Two items, both forecast at 1,000 a week. One needs 285 units of safety stock, the other 1,245.

A single-number forecast can't tell them apart. Item A sells 1,000 give or take 80. Item B swings by 350. Give both a week of cover and you overstock A while B runs out one week in twenty.

Forecast the range instead, and set each item's stock from its own range. Total safety stock falls 24% and B stays in stock 98% of weeks.

Now B's biggest customer moves to monthly orders. The average doesn't move, so the point forecast doesn't either. The range doubles, and B's stock follows to 2,465 units.

Which of your items look identical in the forecast but behave nothing alike?

Invented numbers, real mechanics. A new planning concept every Tuesday and Thursday.
